scope: Read-only source audit of historical Mac capture admission. No compiler, capture, remote, Git, GUI, or production-source execution was performed.
conclusion: Existing candidate and closure policy blocks automatic historical promotion, but Mac pipeline validation has no compiler-OS-origin receipt requirement. A future caller that supplies an old Mac artifact through a bound host/capture adapter can satisfy current generic Mac source/binary checks without proving its compiler invocation. Fresh actual-v1 compiler receipts remain separate evidence; this audit does not re-review them.

existingBarriers.finding: Mac starts candidate-only; candidate generation, receipt generation, or pass verdict cannot promote. Accepted golden requires exact case/tuple plus maintainer-bound candidate/diff/reviewer/timestamp/decision. Headless evidence cannot grant parity.
Capture requires final bound tuple10 plus explicit CLOSED status. Old captures remain historical bytes with no rebinding; plan requires fresh captures and fresh internal scratch.

Closure binds changed runtime, postclosure measurements, and new platform host bytes; candidate summary marks parity false and requires new Mac/Windows captures. closure_check states hosts bind newly built factory hosts, never old archives.

acceptingPathAndGap.finding: validate_host_receipt checks Mac platform, tupleIndependent, runtime commit, postclosure timing, closure links, source bytes, and binary bytes. Compiler receipt fields are required only inside the Windows branch at lines 82-110; Mac has no compiler OS-origin check.

Mac qualification host invokes xcrun swiftc and persists build stdout/stderr through logged(), but host-measurement.json contains source/adapter/compiledAdapter/binary/toolchain/inventory fields, with no compiler receipt path/hash, argv identity, process timing, exit record, or raw stream hashes.

Legacy/current Mac candidate builds log plain stdout/stderr and summary marks candidateOnly/not-promoted. Fresh AX build likewise stores source/binary identity without compiler-origin receipt. No source-level rejection distinguishes old capture build evidence from current receipt-backed build evidence.

Evidence verifier checks capture/raw/image hashes, independent PIDs, font resource joins, AX owner hash, and candidateOnly. It does not inspect compiler receipt existence, provenance, or OS-origin fields.

Plan text says pipeline validates a raw receipt hash, while measure_host output shown above does not emit a compiler receipt field. This is an implementation-contract mismatch to resolve before any future Mac promotion gate.

minimalFactoryOnlyGuard.where: Add Mac-specific admission validation before tuple host binding and before selecting captures for any promotion-capable bundle; keep candidate observation path available.
minimalFactoryOnlyGuard.historicalPolicy: Reject historical Mac capture or host artifacts lacking receipt-backed build lineage as promotion inputs. Keep them observational/candidate-only; never reconstruct missing compiler OS origin.
requiredReceipt: exact xcrun/swiftc argv plus logical argv0 and resolved compiler path
compiler path/tool identity and pre/post hashes
owned PID/PGID, UTC start/end, natural exit code, timeout=false, drained stdout/stderr
receipt path/hash archived under same fresh internal run and joined to bound host/capture
minimalFactoryOnlyGuard.compatibility: Do not alter existing candidate evidence, old bytes, or public/runtime APIs. Guard only promotion-capable Mac host/capture selection.

notClaimed: No fresh compiler or capture run was executed.
No causal performance or parity conclusion is drawn.
Fresh actual-v1 receipt review is treated as separate existing evidence, not repeated here.
No historical compiler receipt is inferred from build stdout/stderr, binary hash, or source hash alone.
